title: Conflict Role Crosswalk — Person × Scene × Source
purpose: Describe recurring conflict mechanisms without converting temporary roles, allegations or literary characterizations into permanent identities.
governing_rules: A person is not a conflict mode.
Roles attach to dated scenes or bounded periods.
Allegations remain attributed to the source that makes them.
Retrospective karmic or prophetic interpretations do not replace the original event record.
Medical outcomes are never treated as caused by symbolic warnings or social metaphors.
Real political/legal cases route to evidence-led case files rather than mythic cast labels.

modes.label: Social Orbit
modes.definition: A second center gathers people, attention, activity or loyalty.

modes.label: Disruption / Raid Pressure
modes.definition: A shared room is flooded, diverted or made harder to govern; each incident needs independent source support.

modes.label: Meta-Framing
modes.definition: Conflict over context, identity, authorship or which narrative becomes authoritative.

modes.label: Boundary Pressure
modes.definition: Bans, filters, servers, doors, follows and cross-community movement make belonging observable.

modes.label: Attribution Conflict
modes.definition: Disagreement over who said, authored, intended or caused an event; requires proposition-level provenance.

modes.label: Aftermath / Metabolization
modes.definition: Conflict is transformed into grief, music, doctrine, humor, repair or new boundaries.
